newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Slow Australian stocks open little changed.
newsitem.headline: Slow Australian stocks open little changed.

text.p: A lightly-traded Australian share market opened little changed on Monday as many traders pinned rate cut hopes to key inflation and wages data due next week.
The All Ordinaries index lost three points to 2,696.1.
Brokers said with many investors already factoring in an interest rate cut, delays could cause disappointment with next week's data keenly watched for portents of any possible change.
"That is dwelling on people's minds a bit," said Phillip Toop, a dealer at Brisbane brokerage, Henderson Charlton Jones.
"Any delay in the rate cut may prove a disappointment to people that have already built it into their expectations."
Among individuals stocks, sugar, building materials and aluminium group CSR Ltd lost eight cents at A$5.19 (US$3.84) despite forecasting an improved full year profit at the annual meeting.

Trade was active in pay TV operator Australis Media on the back of renewed rumours of a merger with rival operator, Foxtel, the pay TV vehicle of News Corp and government owned telecommunications carrier, Telstra Corp. Australis shares added 1.5 cents to 15.5 cents with 3.2 million shares traded.
After volatile trade in the last week, the gold sector was steady with mixed performances and no discernible trend.
Rises outnumbered falls by a ratio of more than two to one, while about 41 percent of stocks traded remained steady.
